page: Microsoft Azure D32d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include Intel AVX-512 extensions with VNNI support. For temporary high-speed data handling, the configuration includes 1288 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage. It features no GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results characterize the instance as a balanced middle-tier compute platform with clear tradeoffs in single-threaded velocity. The instance scored 1,413.36 in stress-ng single-core tests and 23.49 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, both ranking in the lower quartile of comparative systems. However, its 32 vCPUs scale predictably in parallel environments, registering average performance across stress-ng multi-core (29,808.15), Geekbench multi-core (10,781.0), and PassMark CPU (27,072.36). Memory subsystems achieve uncached large-block read speeds of 105.49 GB/sec and write speeds of 46.46 GB/sec. While functional for lightweight CPU-based language model inference on smaller models, larger architectures such as 70B models reveal severe bottlenecks due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

In terms of resource economics, the D32d_v4 provides consistent multi-core density coupled with substantial fast local SSD storage without requiring external persistent disk provision for ephemeral data. This architecture fits workloads demanding symmetrical compute and memory capacity combined with fast temporary workspace. Primary workload applications include relational and in-memory databases, caching nodes like Redis (which demonstrated 26.79 million SET operations per second), enterprise web application tiers, Clang-based software compilation pipelines, and batch ETL data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D32d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1288 GB local SSD. It includes no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and caching operations within the median tier, achieving 27,072.36 on PassMark CPU and 26.79 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, while single-core execution speed registers in the lower quartile. The integrated local SSD eliminates latency for temporary files and fast scratch space. D32d_v4 accommodates enterprise application servers, mid-tier database hosting, software compilation pipelines, and scalable web serving environments requiring a balanced compute-to-memory footprint.
